concept: One work laptop and one phone on a quiet desk, the whole lesson on a single generic browser shell: Sam's leaked password is a chip that gets in at the start and is stopped at the code screen at the end; in between the pointer walks every click of turning on two-step sign-in, using a password manager and recovering from a lost phone.

devices.what: the work laptop's browser app shell (W.app, browser chrome, generic company account site), held across each chapter with W.resume; pages change with A.go, the camera zooms on each named control

the authenticator phone (kit part), standing to the right of the laptop shell; one phone with states: app home with Add account, camera framing the QR, account row with a six-digit code and a 30 s ring, missing, and a second new phone
Sam's masked password as a small chip (kit part): typed in the hook, slips out of the leaked shop, comes back in b06 and the payoff and is stopped at the code step
the teaching layer in accent2: chapter pills for the four chapters, the step pill per walkthrough step, and the numbered lost-phone path held on the left in b21 and b22
join material: handoff (the next chapter's window grows in from the held one) at chapter changes; continue inside a chapter

value_script.why: pale open on the quiet desk
slightly richer middle: zoomed walkthroughs, the lost-phone dim and the recovery path
lift at the close: the stopped attempt in a spotlight, the checklist ticked

beats.line: Two browser windows side by side, a shop and the company sign-in; the same masked password typed into both
The shop window cracks, the password chip slips out, a stranger's pointer types it into the company sign-in, Sign in, the inbox opens
The company window becomes a settings card with two toggles, Two-step sign-in and Password manager, both switching on
Three tiles on the desk light as named: one key opening several sign-ins, a look-alike sign-in page, a scrolling list of masked passwords
The sign-in page gains a code step; the phone stands beside it showing a code; two labels, Something you know and Something you have
A stranger's pointer types the stolen chip; the page moves to the code step and waits, no way forward
Walkthrough: account menu, Security, scroll to Two-step sign-in, click Turn on, each control zoomed
Method picker dialog; click Authenticator app; a QR code fades in
The phone slides in beside the laptop; tap Add account; the camera view frames the QR
The phone shows the account with a six-digit code and a ring that runs out and refreshes
The code typed into the laptop's code box matching the phone; click Verify; success tick
Backup codes panel; one code highlighted and called out as single use
The codes lift off; the phone crossed out on one side; they settle into a password manager vault card with an IT note
The password manager window grows in: one master password field, the vault opens onto saved logins
A short password in the unlock field grows into a long passphrase; the strength bar fills
A generic site sign-in in the browser; the manager's Save prompt drops down; click Save; the login joins the vault list
The site's Change password form; click Generate; a long random password fills the field
Save; later the sign-in page fills itself; the address bar called out
Two browser windows: the real address fills itself in, a look-alike address with one letter changed stays empty and is flagged as a warning sign
The phone's spot is empty; the laptop shows the code step waiting under a dim
A numbered path on the left: 1 a backup code typed into the code box, 2 a message to IT
The same path continues: 3 the new phone scans a QR, 4 the old device removed from the device list and other sessions signed out
The Two-step sign-in toggle pulled toward off, marked wrong; the code moves from the old phone to the new, marked right
The hook's stranger pointer types the leaked chip into the company sign-in; the page halts on the code step while Sam's phone holds the code
Three checklist items tick off over the laptop and the phone
